findings.suggested_fix: State the testable part: a warning indicator is present when No-show count >= 2 and absent when < 2.
findings.text: REQ-13 'highlighted as a warning' gives a tester no observable condition; the style is deferred to design, but the REQ could state what must be distinguishable (e.g. a warning indicator present only when count >= 2).

rubric_items.reason: All eight acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-18; out-of-scope items carry reasons.
Mostly atomic and checkable; REQ-2 bundles the content list and REQ-13 'highlighted as a warning' has no checkable condition beyond deferral to design.
Statuses cite ticket lines or A-01; REQ-8 adds 'without a time', an inference beyond the ticket text, still marked known.
The only baseline clash (time zone hard-coded vs Settings) was asked, answered in A-01 and recorded as a mismatch citing the baseline.
One question, routed to an engineer, with real options; no needless blocking.
Plain wording; Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled, No-show and Medical history used as in the glossary.
